subject: Electrical Engineering
title: PID Tuning: Finding the Right Gains
description: A 60-second lesson on PID Tuning: Finding the Right Gains.

hook.text: A PID controller has three knobs: Kp, Ki, Kd. Setting them right is an art and a science.

buildup.text: The Ziegler-Nichols method: increase Kp until oscillation, then set Ki and Kd from formulas.

discovery.text: This gives a starting point — engineers then fine-tune by observing the step response.

twist.text: Auto-tuning algorithms now measure the system response and compute PID gains automatically.

climax.text: Well-tuned PID reaches the setpoint fast, with minimal overshoot and no oscillation.

punchline.text: Three gains, one goal — balance speed, accuracy, and stability.

quiz.question: What does the Ziegler-Nichols tuning method start with?
options: Setting all three gains to maximum and reducing gradually
Increasing proportional gain until the system oscillates steadily
Running the system in open-loop and measuring the output
